title: Building Block One: The Leader's Seven Essential Behaviors
coreMove: Convert leadership intent into visible behaviors that make realism and follow-through unavoidable.
sourcePressure: First building block: execution becomes concrete through seven leader behaviors, from knowing people and the business to realism, priorities, follow-through, doer rewards, coaching, self-knowledge, and emotional fortitude. No chapter-specific named case study is frozen.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Summarize leadership traits as personality advice detached from execution.

hook: the building block one: the leader's seven essential behaviors that nobody sees until it is too late
a meeting room where every plan sounds good
a generic promise colliding with reality
counterintuition: Most leaders think X, but the opposite is true
The problem is not effort, it is discipline
Execution is not about working harder
tryThisNow: set a timer and write three priorities
audit one goal in your notebook
ask yourself what matters most today
examples: generic project kickoff with vague owners
student team with a deadline and no specificity
family calendar scene used as a management analogy

exampleSpecs.domain: a fire captain reviewing a warehouse alarm response after a near miss
exampleSpecs.audience: a frontline leader who has been relying on secondhand summaries
exampleSpecs.stakes: a repeated blind spot can injure the crew on the next call
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah leaves the office summary and walks the apparatus bay until direct knowledge of people and equipment changes the after-action decision
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The apparatus bay smells like wet canvas while Hannah studies the cracked coupling on engine two.

exampleSpecs.domain: a university debate coach choosing final tournament priorities after a crowded prep week
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach whose team wants to practice everything
exampleSpecs.stakes: scattered practice can leave the weakest round untouched
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael names two priorities and crosses four others off the prep board so follow-through has a chance
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "We are not rehearsing six things tonight," Michael says, marker cap in his palm.

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique hotel manager deciding who gets praised after a difficult conference weekend
exampleSpecs.audience: a service manager shaping standards through recognition
exampleSpecs.stakes: the staff will learn whether visible charm or carried-through work earns status
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chloe rewards the night auditor who solved room-key failures instead of the host who made the lobby look smooth
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The key-card encoder is still warm when Chloe reaches the morning huddle.

exampleSpecs.domain: a youth orchestra rehearsal where the conductor has to coach without lowering the bar
exampleSpecs.audience: a conductor developing capable section leaders
exampleSpecs.stakes: soft feedback will preserve comfort but not the concert standard
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Matthew points to the exact measure, asks the violin lead to hear the entry again, and keeps the standard clear while coaching
exampleSpecs.firstImage: At 7:06 p.m., Matthew taps measure 42 on the score and waits for the violins to settle.

exampleSpecs.domain: a freight dispatch center where a supervisor hears only the safe version of a missed pickup
exampleSpecs.audience: a supervisor trying to insist on realism
exampleSpecs.stakes: a retailer can lose the holiday delivery slot if the true bottleneck stays hidden
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jonas asks which fact the team is avoiding, predicts the missing constraint, and rewards the dispatcher who names it plainly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which sentence is missing from a dispatch report that says the route is under review?

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit grant team where the director notices pride bending the numbers
exampleSpecs.audience: a director who must know himself before correcting the team
exampleSpecs.stakes: a flattering report can put next-year funding at risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Aman catches his own desire for a clean narrative before asking the team to revise the report around the uncomfortable data
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You want the funder report to be true because Aman has already pictured the renewal call.

skillTargets: recognize the seven behaviors in visible leadership actions
choose realism over comfort in status moments
distinguish coaching that expands capability from lowering standards
evaluate reward signals after execution work

tryThisNowSpec: Name one behavior you will inspect today: direct knowledge, realism, priority, follow-through, reward, coaching, or self-control.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
